title: Sequentially Indifferentiable Block Cipher with Linear Simulation
summary: The four-round IEM construction is sequentially indifferentiable but uses a quadratic-query simulator; finding a linear-query construction with optimal chosen-key resistance remains open.

formal_statement.body: Construct a block cipher from an underlying primitive such as a random oracle or a small set of random permutations, with the construction being sequentially indifferentiable from an ideal cipher and having a simulator whose query complexity is linear. The unresolved goal is additionally required to yield optimal resistance to chosen-key attacks, which the stated composition result says would follow from the requested sequential indifferentiability and linear simulator complexity.

scope.domain: Block-cipher design from idealized primitives, with security measured by sequential indifferentiability and chosen-key resistance.
parameters: Underlying primitive: a random oracle or a small set of random permutations used to construct the block cipher
Simulator query complexity: the resource measure required to be linear
scope.unresolved_remainder: Construct a block cipher that is sequentially indifferentiable from an ideal cipher with linear simulator query complexity, so that the composition result yields optimal chosen-key resistance.

citations.label: On the Provable Security of the Iterated Even-Mansour Cipher Against Related-Key and Chosen-Key Attacks

progress.summary: The source presents its sequentially indifferentiable four-round IEM construction, whose simulator has quadratic query complexity, as falling short of the desired chosen-key guarantee. It explicitly asks for linear simulator complexity and states that its composition theorem would then imply optimal chosen-key resistance.
citation_labels: Benoît Cogliati et al., On the Provable Security of the Iterated Even-Mansour Cipher Against Related-Key and Chosen-Key Attacks
